sample_data.reset_instructions: Click Reset published fixture in the header to restore all 25 cases and select PUB-01.

problem_solving_method: Integer-poisha tariff functions allocate each day across calendar-month slabs. The same ledger results feed the balance trace, run-out forecast, deposit advice and habit comparison.

R1.proof: The selected case shows its light month, heavy summer month and largest late-week recharge. The bundled fixture contains 25 six-month cases.

R2.proof: The chart marks every recharge. The full ledger shows opening balance, calendar-month units, slab allocation, recharge, BDT 82 first-recharge fixed charge, energy, VAT and closing balance. The full ledger is downloadable as CSV.

R3.proof: The route gives the run-out date and reconciles the target-date deposit into first-slab energy, higher-slab increment, VAT, applicable fixed charges and balance credit.

R4.proof: Both policies use identical daily consumption and the same calendar-month slab counter. Energy and VAT must match exactly. Consumed cost, deposits and balances are kept separate, and both policy summaries are downloadable as CSV.

evaluated_forecast.proof: A 30-day holdout compares regularized regression with a 7-day mean baseline. The lower-RMSE model is selected automatically and produces a 90 percent confidence band.

alerts_and_anomalies.proof: Each anomaly states the reading, trailing average, deviation and configured sigma threshold. Budget and run-out alerts expose editable thresholds and calculation reasons.

appliance_simulator.proof: Wattage, hours, quantity and current use feed the same slab rates and daily VAT rounding. Fixed-charge evidence stays separate, and 5, 10 and 20 percent scenarios show units and money saved.

safe_json_import.proof: Validation covers calendar dates, schema, problem, comparison inputs, malformed JSON, file type and a 5 MiB pre-read limit. Invalid input preserves the active fixture.

verification.latest_result: 65 tests passed; TypeScript, ESLint and the Next.js 16.3.3 production build completed successfully.

major_design_decisions: Represent money as integer poisha and split a day across every crossed slab.
Apply start-of-day recharge and the month's first fixed charges before that day's consumption.
Reuse the tariff and ledger functions across all four requirements.
Keep consumed cost separate from deposits and test exact energy and VAT equality.
Parse judge JSON locally and provide reset without a backend.
known_limitations: Imported fixture state and table state do not persist across a full refresh.
The whole-unit reading schema rejects fractional daily units.
VAT is rounded per daily energy charge to the nearest poisha because no other interval is specified.
